title: All three at once: the wiring proved by seam, the listings found stacking beside the reads, and a starved GCD queue billed to the Keychain
problem: Three open threads from previous rounds: the restack guard had no wiring proof, the 286-second securityd block was unidentified, and keychain.queue.starved had never been examined. All three were taken in one round.
findings: WHERE THE BLOCK WAS. keychain.queue.starved fired zero times during the 286s stall. That signal measures how long a dispatched block waits for a GCD slot, so its absence says scheduling was prompt and the wait was inside SecItemCopyMatching. A signal that did not fire is evidence when you know what would have made it fire.

WHAT QUEUED BEHIND IT. Four keychain.enumeration.stalled at +68.3s, +137.2s, +206.2s and +274.9s - spacing 68.9 / 69.0 / 68.7, the same cooldown cadence as the five reads, on the same service, interleaved with them. Listings and reads were one pile-up through two code paths. The guard written earlier today covered only the reads.

A STALL THAT WAS NOT ONE. Across 59 starvation events: median slot wait 0.41s, max 7.05s, five longer than the caller's entire two-second deadline. For those five SecItemCopyMatching was never reached, and the timeout path still said 'did not answer in 2s' and armed sixty seconds of refusals.
keychain.enumeration.stalled had never been examined by any round, despite being in the signal list since it was written.

make check has two locks on the same resource with opposite policies: the cassette step WAITS for /tmp/trios_harness.lock, check-selftest FAILS on it. That is why a concurrent run sometimes hangs for fifty minutes and sometimes goes red in seconds.
fix: The enumeration path now uses the same KeychainReadStacking decision under its own key, so a stalled listing does not refuse keyed reads of that service. A read whose block waited longer than the whole deadline reports keychain.read.starved_out and arms no cooldown. keychain_restack_wiring_test seeds outstandingReads directly - the field is module-internal for that purpose and says so in its own doc comment - and drives the refusal, the settle, the abandonment that must not latch, and the key separation. wasStarvedOut is a pure decision with four checks.
prevention: When you find a defect in one path, grep for the SHAPE rather than the symbol. The enumeration path was a near-copy of the read path and contains the word 'read' nowhere.
A signal that did not fire is evidence, but only when you can say what would have made it fire. Otherwise absence is just absence.

A guard against inventing causes can invent one. wasStarvedOut returns false for a nil slot wait because a block that never started recorded nothing, and the tempting reading - 'it must have been starved' - is the same defect wearing the fix's clothes.

Do not ship a branch and its proof in different rounds. Two of the three new signals had a decision suite and a wiring suite; the third had neither until it was pointed out, in a round about exactly this.

proof_status.keychain.read.not_restacked: decision proved (11 checks), wiring proved (8 checks, seeded state), NOT observed live
proof_status.keychain.enumeration.not_restacked: decision proved (shares the same function), wiring proved under its own key, NOT observed live
proof_status.keychain.read.starved_out: decision proved (4 checks), wiring NOT proved, NOT observed live
proof_status.why_none_are_live: The launch window after the release build was healthy - 3 stalls, 3 settles, 0 starvation, 0 enumeration stalls - so none of the three conditions occurred. All three need securityd to be slow or the queue to be saturated in that minute, which a round cannot arrange.

corrections_to_earlier_claims: Previous rounds treated the 286-second block as unexplained. It is still unexplained as to CAUSE, but its LOCATION is now established: inside the Security call, not in GCD scheduling, on the evidence of queue.starved firing zero times in the window.
I recommended in the previous round that the restack guard was the fix for the pile-up. It was half the fix: the listings were stacking on the same cadence and were not covered.
